# real-enums

> Enums that are real classes, for TypeScript, Ember and React. Each value is a static
> member; labels, CSS classes and transitions are getters on it. Adapters turn the strings an
> API sends into members for WarpDrive/ember-data, TanStack Query, SWR, RTK Query, Apollo and
> urql. `Cls.match(value)` branches on a member with the compiler checking every member is
> handled.

Install the core package, `npm i @real-enums/core`, and import from `@real-enums/core`. The
data-layer adapters are `@real-enums/warp-drive`, `@real-enums/tanstack-query`,
`@real-enums/swr`, `@real-enums/rtk-query`, `@real-enums/apollo` and `@real-enums/urql`.

## Rules for writing code with real-enums

1. Declare members with `Cls.of('value')`, never `new Cls('value')`. `of` gives each member
   its own type, which `match` needs; an enum with a `new` member cannot be matched. Extra
   constructor arguments follow the value: `Icon.of('open', '🟢')`.
2. When every member needs an answer, use `Cls.match(value)` and end with `.exhaustive()`.
   Do not write `if`/`else` chains, `switch` statements or lookup tables over members for
   this: TypeScript cannot check them, so a new member is silently missed. Tables keyed by
   `value` (like `next` in the example) are for lookups only some members answer.
3. Cases are static members (`OrderState.Pending`), never strings (`'pending'`). One `.when`
   takes several members: `.when([OrderState.Pending, OrderState.Shipped], fn)`.
4. Use `.otherwise(fn)` only when a fallback is truly intended. It turns the exhaustiveness
   check off for that match.
5. Compare members with `===` or a predicate (`state.isPending`), not with their string value.
6. Put behaviour that belongs to the value (label, CSS class, next state) in a getter on the
   class, not in the template or component.
7. A type error from `match` names the member to handle. Fix it by handling that member;
   never with a cast, `any`, `@ts-ignore` or `@ts-expect-error`.
8. Raw strings from an API become members through the data layer's adapter, or
   `mapFields`/`Cls.codec()`. Do not call `Cls.valueFor` by hand in every component.

## Example

```ts
import { Enum, is, isNot } from '@real-enums/core'

export class OrderState extends Enum {
  static Pending = OrderState.of('pending')
  static Shipped = OrderState.of('shipped')
  static Delivered = OrderState.of('delivered')
  static Cancelled = OrderState.of('cancelled')

  @is() accessor isPending!: boolean
  @is() accessor isCancelled!: boolean
  @isNot() accessor isNotCancelled!: boolean

  get next(): OrderState | undefined {
    return {
      [OrderState.Pending.value]: OrderState.Shipped,
      [OrderState.Shipped.value]: OrderState.Delivered,
    }[this.value]
  }

  get advanceLabel(): string | undefined {
    return {
      [OrderState.Pending.value]: 'Ship',
      [OrderState.Shipped.value]: 'Deliver',
    }[this.value]
  }

  get className() {
    return `badge badge--${this.value}`
  }
}
```

Every member handled, two of them in one case:

```ts
const statusText = (state: OrderState) =>
  OrderState.match(state)
    .when([OrderState.Pending, OrderState.Shipped], () => 'In progress')
    .when([OrderState.Delivered], () => 'Done')
    .when([OrderState.Cancelled], () => 'Cancelled')
    .exhaustive()
```

A deliberate fallback:

```ts
const canEdit = (state: OrderState) =>
  OrderState.match(state)
    .when([OrderState.Pending], () => true)
    .otherwise(() => false)
```

In Ember apps, which compile legacy decorators, predicates are written
`@is() declare isPending: boolean`.

## Docs

- [Guide](https://joegaudet.com/real-enums/guide/): declaring enums, predicates, exhaustive
  matching, data layers, validation and the API
- [Package README](https://github.com/joegaudet/real-enums/tree/main/packages/real-enums#readme):
  the full API, including upgrading from 1.x
- [Adapter setup](https://joegaudet.com/real-enums/#ember): Ember and React data layers
- [Examples](https://github.com/joegaudet/real-enums/tree/main/examples): one app per data
  layer
